cd /testbed && printf '%s
' '{"title":"Title 1","media:content":{"media:credits":"media:content.media:credits 1"}}' | ./jq '{title, credits: .["media:content"].["media:credits"]}'; printf '
--- parser index rules ---
'; rg -n 'yyerror|Term|INDEX|gen_index|gen_slice' src/parser.y; sed -n '1,100p' tests/jq.test; git --no-pager diff --stat && ls docs/content && rg -n 'Object Identifier|Generic Object|\.\["foo"\]|Array.*Slice' docs/content/manual*

cd /testbed && grep -nE 'yyerror|Term|gen_index|gen_slice' src/parser.y && sed -n '600,750p' src/parser.y && git --no-pager diff -- src/parser.c | head -100 && grep -nE 'yyerror|syntax error|Term.*\[' src/parser.c | tail -35 && find docs/content/manual -maxdepth 2 -type f && grep -nE 'Object Identifier|Generic Object|\.\["foo"\]|Array.*Slice' docs/content/manual/*
cd /testbed && ./jq -n '.foo.["bar"]' && file jq && sed -n '1,180p' /opt/peeky/docs/lang/c-cpp.md && grep -nE 'jq.test|TESTS|check-local|JQTEST' Makefile.am tests/* 2>/dev/null | head -75

cd /testbed && git --no-pager log -4 --oneline && git --no-pager show HEAD:src/parser.y | sed -n '685,715p' && grep -nE '\.\[|#.*[Ii]ndex|#.*[Ss]lice' tests/jq.test | head -65 && sed -n '345,475p' docs/content/manual/manual.yml && sed -n '390,425p' src/parser.c && sed -n '3190,3238p' src/parser.c && sed -n '3750,3808p' src/parser.c && sed -n '1,95p' tests/setup && command -v peeky

cd /testbed && peeky probe . --binary ./jq --at src/parser.c:3218 --capture yyn,yylen,yystate,yychar -- -n '{"title":"Title 1","media:content":{"media:credits":"media:content.media:credits 1"}} | {title, credits: .["media:content"].["media:credits"]}'

cd /testbed && apply_patch <<'PATCH'
*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: tests/jq.test
@@
 .["foo"].bar
 {"foo": {"bar": 42}, "bar": "badvalue"}
 42
 
+# Generic object indexes can be chained, with or without a separating dot.
+[.["foo"].["bar"], .foo.["bar"], .["foo"]["bar"], .foo.bar, (.foo | .bar)]
+{"foo": {"bar": 42}, "bar": "badvalue"}
+[42,42,42,42,42]
+
+{title, credits: .["media:content"].["media:credits"]}
+{"title":"Title 1","media:content":{"media:credits":"media:content.media:credits 1"}}
+{"title":"Title 1","credits":"media:content.media:credits 1"}
+
+.["foo"].[("b" + "ar"), "baz"]
+{"foo":{"bar":42,"baz":43}}
+42
+43
+
+[.[] | .["foo"]?.["bar"]?]
+[1,[],{"foo":1},{"foo":[]},{"foo":{"bar":42}},{"foo":{}},{}]
+[42,null,null]
+
+[.[] | .foo.["bar"]?]
+[{"foo":1},{"foo":[]},{"foo":{"bar":42}},{"foo":{}},{}]
+[42,null,null]
+
+.["foo"].[1].["bar"]
+{"foo":[{"bar":41},{"bar":42}]}
+42
+
+path(.["foo"].["bar"])
+{"foo":{"bar":42}}
+["foo","bar"]
+
+.["foo"].["bar"] |= . + 1
+{"foo":{"bar":42}}
+{"foo":{"bar":43}}
+
 ."foo"."bar"
 {"foo": {"bar": 20}}
 20
*** Update File: docs/content/manual/manual.yml
@@
           `.foo::bar` does not, and `.foo.bar` means `.["foo"].["bar"]`.
+
+          Bracket indexes can be chained with or without a separating dot:
+          `.["foo"].["bar"]`, `.["foo"]["bar"]`, and `.foo.["bar"]`
+          are equivalent to `.foo.bar`.
@@
           - program: '.["foo"]'
             input: '{"foo": 42}'
             output: [42]
+          - program: '.["media:content"].["media:credits"]'
+            input: '{"media:content": {"media:credits": "credit"}}'
+            output: ['"credit"']
*** End Patch
PATCH
make -j4 && make check

cd /testbed && python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
path = Path('tests/jq.test')
text = path.read_text()
old = '''.["foo"].bar
{"foo": {"bar": 42}, "bar": "badvalue"}
42

'''
new = old + '''# Generic object indexes can be chained, with or without a separating dot.
+[.["foo"].["bar"], .foo.["bar"], .["foo"]["bar"], .foo.bar, (.foo | .bar)]
+{"foo": {"bar": 42}, "bar": "badvalue"}
+[42,42,42,42,42]
+
+{title, credits: .["media:content"].["media:credits"]}
+{"title":"Title 1","media:content":{"media:credits":"media:content.media:credits 1"}}
+{"title":"Title 1","credits":"media:content.media:credits 1"}
+
+.["foo"].[("b" + "ar"), "baz"]
+{"foo":{"bar":42,"baz":43}}
+42
+43
+
+[.[] | .["foo"]?.["bar"]?]
+[1,[],{"foo":1},{"foo":[]},{"foo":{"bar":42}},{"foo":{}},{}]
+[42,null,null]
+
+[.[] | .foo.["bar"]?]
+[{"foo":1},{"foo":[]},{"foo":{"bar":42}},{"foo":{}},{}]
+[42,null,null]
+
+.["foo"].[1].["bar"]
+{"foo":[{"bar":41},{"bar":42}]}
+42
+
+path(.["foo"].["bar"])
+{"foo":{"bar":42}}
+["foo","bar"]
+
+.["foo"].["bar"] |= . + 1
+{"foo":{"bar":42}}
+{"foo":{"bar":43}}
+
+'''.replace('\n+', '\n')
assert text.count(old) == 1
path.write_text(text.replace(old, new))
path = Path('docs/content/manual/manual.yml')
text = path.read_text()
old = '''          `.foo::bar` does not, and `.foo.bar` means `.["foo"].["bar"]`.
'''
new = old + '''
          Bracket indexes can be chained with or without a separating dot:
          `.["foo"].["bar"]`, `.["foo"]["bar"]`, and `.foo.["bar"]`
          are equivalent to `.foo.bar`.
'''
assert text.count(old) == 1
text = text.replace(old, new)
old = '''          - program: '.["foo"]'
            input: '{"foo": 42}'
            output: [42]
'''
new = old + '''          - program: '.["media:content"].["media:credits"]'
            input: '{"media:content": {"media:credits": "credit"}}'
            output: ['"credit"']
'''
assert text.count(old) == 1
path.write_text(text.replace(old, new))
PY
make -s -j4 && make -s check

cd /testbed && git --no-pager diff --check && git --no-pager diff -- tests/jq.test docs/content/manual/manual.yml && git --no-pager status --short && printf '%s\n' '{"media:content":{"media:credits":"credit"}}' | ./jq -ce '.["media:content"].["media:credits"] == "credit"' && tail -5 tests/jqtest.log
